candidate.title: The shell key-material rule lets a hunter read ~/.aws/cli/cache and ~/.aws/sso/cache that the file-tool rule denies
candidate.description: The file-tool rule in hooks/qa-guardrail denies the whole `.aws/` folder. The shell rule isKeyMaterial (guard-paths.mjs) names only `.aws/credentials`, and the bash text rule at :1143 does the same. The hunt allows cat, head, grep and similar on paths outside the project, so a prompt-injected hunter can read the AWS CLI's cached role credentials and SSO access tokens through the shell and put them in its context or in a committed reviews/<id>/ file, while the Read tool refuses the same file.
candidate.claimed_root_cause: Two copies of the key list disagree: the file-tool KEY_RE uses `(^|/)\.aws(/|$)` and the shared isKeyMaterial uses `\.aws\/credentials`, although the comment on isKeyMaterial says it is the same list as the hook's shell rule.

trace.description: A shell word such as ~/.aws/cli/cache/token.json is judged by text only, because a `~` word is not 'plain' (:1561).
isKeyMaterial(keyText(word)) is the only key-name test for the word.
The shell copy of the key list matches `.aws/credentials` but not `.aws/cli/cache/*` or `.aws/sso/cache/*`.
cat, head, tail and grep are on the hunt's program list and read any path, so the file is printed.

evidence.description: The file-tool KEY_RE denies `(^|/)\.aws(/|$)`, so the Read tool refuses the same file the shell reads.
The bash text rule over the command also names only `.aws/credentials`.
The comment claims the list is the same as the hook's shell rule; the two regexes differ.
keyGlobReaches (guard-paths.mjs:121) lists only .aws/credentials among the AWS names, so a glob such as ~/.aws/cli/cache/*.json is not caught either.

blockers: No sandbox for this run, so the analyzer was not executed on `cat ~/.aws/sso/cache/x.json`
Whether the developer's machine holds a populated ~/.aws/cli/cache or ~/.aws/sso/cache is a deployment fact

validation_plan.local: In a throwaway project with a hunt run record, feed hooks/qa-guardrail `cat ~/.aws/sso/cache/a.json` through Bash and `~/.aws/sso/cache/a.json` through Read, and compare: the shell call is expected to be allowed and the Read call denied.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner check: list ~/.aws/cli/cache and ~/.aws/sso/cache on the hunting machine to see whether live credentials sit there; if so, align both lists on the whole `.aws/` folder.

checks.invariant: isKeyMaterial is the same key list as the hook's file-tool rule, and its move out of qa-shell-writes.mjs changed no behaviour
checks.result: git diff dev..GH-63-cloudflare-engine shows the KEY_RE removed from qa-shell-writes.mjs and added to guard-paths.mjs byte for byte, with every caller switched to isKeyMaterial (:1356, :1532, :1536, :1575, :2287), so the move is behaviour-neutral. The list is not the same as the file-tool rule in hooks/qa-guardrail:637, although the comment at guard-paths.mjs:177 claims it is: the file-tool regex denies the whole `.aws/` folder, the shell version only `.aws/credentials`. A read of `~/.aws/cli/cache/*.json` or `~/.aws/sso/cache/*.json` (cached temporary credentials and SSO bearer tokens) is therefore denied through the Read tool and allowed through `cat` (candidate hunt-guardrail/key-material-aws-cache-weaker-in-shell-rule). The 8.3 and symlink resolution in checkAlias (:1559-1576) is correct for in-project words, but a `~` word is judged by text only (`plain` is false).

checks.invariant: a key-material path field or glob in any hunt tool call is denied before the hunt's tool gate and the write rules
checks.result: The node block collects every path-shaped field and glob field (:471-490), and the bash block denies a KEY_RE match on the typed and the real spelling (:647-664) and on a glob that can expand to a key name (:666), before the hunt gate (:767) and the file-tool gate (:873). `.env.example` is stripped deliberately. A tool with an unreadable path or a twotargets call is denied (:550, :589-593). No bypass found for the tools the hunt gate lets through.
